_reasons.global-state: jce_engine_set_target_fps holds one process-global frame-cap object (fps + deadline, together because changing one without the other misaligns the next frame). It is process-global for the same reason jce_engine_set_fixed_hz is: JceServices carries no JceEngine handle, so a game's app_init has no engine pointer to pass, and the setter must work before the engine exists. Adding an engine handle to JceServices would let every app reach into the engine -- a much larger hole than one static.  ||  jce_lighting_set_pixel_light_count holds one process-global int (the per-pixel light budget). Process-global for the same reason as the frame cap and jce_texture_set_quality_mip_bias: a shipped game applies it in app_init, before any scene renderer exists, and JceServices carries no handle to pass instead.  ||  global-state 853 -> 854: one file-static, s_particles_soft_fade in jce_particles.c, holding the soft-particle fade distance.  It sits directly beside s_particles_max_dt and is the same shape as jce_lighting_set_pixel_light_count's global -- both already inside the 853.  A quality-level knob has to be process-global here: the shipped drop-in main applies it while parsing render_settings.json, before any renderer or scene exists, and the editor viewport and Play session write the same value from the same quality level.  ||  global-state 854 -> 855: g_cap in jce_scene_probe_capture.c, the single-slot reflection-probe capture state.  Single-slot by design and the same shape as g_bake in jce_impostor.c, already inside the 854: at most one bake may be in flight, both because the read-back staging buffer is shared and because the capture is modal (both editor viewports yield to it).  IT APPEARED ONE COMMIT LATE: find_duplicate_symbols.py enumerates sources with 'git ls-files', so the file was invisible to the detector while untracked and the audit that ran beside it was green on a tree that already contained it.  ||  global-state 855 -> 857: two file-statics, each sitting beside the state it extends.  s_history_edit_scope_entity in jce_editor_history.cpp joins s_history_edit_nesting / s_history_outer_edit_pushed_snapshot -- the module is one instance of edit state by design, and the scope is one more field of it.  s_insp_edit_scope in jce_panel_inspector_common.cpp joins s_insp_batch_open, and exists for the same reason that one does: insp_track_edit() is called from ~490 widget sites with no context, so the entity has to reach it out of band.  Passing it as a parameter instead would mean editing every one of those call sites.  ||  UV tiling reaches a glTF draw: +1 bgfx uniform handle (s_u_uv_transform, the ninth in jce_pbr_material.c and the same shape as the other eight) and +1 per-draw override (s_uv_override, merged from two statics into one by using x<=0 as the disarmed sentinel -- a zero tiling collapses every map to one texel and so cannot be a value anyone means). The override exists because a glTF model draws with the materials the ASSET carries, so the renderer's tiling reached nothing at all on the most common authoring shape in this tree: measured, tiling 1->4 on 1789 renderers moved 4046 px against a 4339 px floor.  ||  2026-09-08 text shape cache: ONE static, and it is the cache. jce_text_shape.c holds a 256-slot table so an unchanged string is shaped once instead of twice per frame; the first version had six loose statics and this detector caught them, which is what folded them into one struct (855->859 became 855->856). The remaining one cannot be folded away, only MOVED: the alternative is a handle threaded through jce_text_draw/measure and every caller of them, in the engine and in every SDK project, to relocate one static out of a subsystem that already keeps s_ft_lib, s_next_sdf_spread, s_text_xf and s_text_style beside it. A process-wide cache with a process-wide lifetime is the honest shape here.  ||  2026-09-17 GPU blendshape deform: TWO file-statics, and each is the smallest shape its job admits.  (1) s_destroy_hook in jce_morph.c is one function pointer -- the seam that lets jce_morph_data_destroy invalidate the pointer-keyed GPU cache WITHOUT jce_morph.c knowing a GPU exists (it is the bgfx-free core precisely so the import/eval path is testable with no renderer).  The alternative was a jce_morph_gpu_release() call at each destroy site, which is two sites in engine/src/renderer/ today -- a layer the morph GPU header may not be included from (check_layer_dependencies) -- and an unknown number tomorrow, each of which would have to remember; a pointer-keyed cache that outlives its key does not fail loudly, it hands the next allocation at that address somebody else's vertices.  (2) s_mg in jce_morph_gpu.c is ONE struct holding the module: the compute program, its three uniforms, the 64-entry per-primitive device-buffer cache and two once-flags.  Process-global because the DELTAS are shared by every instance of a model -- that sharing is the feature, since the CPU path it replaces kept a full per-instance vertex copy -- and folded into one struct rather than left as six names, which is the shape this detector taught the text shape cache two weeks ago.  ||  2026-09-18 static-batch member culling: ONE file-static, s_draw_runs in jce_model.c -- the index runs armed for the next model draw, folded into one struct (first[], count[], n) rather than left as three names, which is the shape this detector taught the text shape cache and the morph GPU module. It sits directly beside s_draw_lod_level, s_pre_submit_cb and s_pre_submit_user, all already inside the 856, and it is the same kind of thing: a per-draw parameter that has to reach the BOTTOM of jce_model_draw_program without every caller in between carrying it. Threading it as a parameter instead would mean changing all fourteen jce_model_draw* entry points and every call site of each -- and the reason it must live at the bottom at all is measured: a static model reaches a draw through several ladders with several exits, and four wirings at individual draw sites each looked right and each reached nothing.  ||  2026-09-20 engine assertions: TWO file-statics, one per module, and each is already the folded form this detector asks for. (1) g_a in engine/src/os/core/jce_assert.c holds the whole facility: the installed handler and its user pointer, the fatal-failure counter, and the 256-entry JCE_ENSURE site table with its state array and count. Process-global because an assertion facility has no instance to hang off -- a JCE_ASSERT fires from code that has no engine, no scene and possibly no main thread, which is the whole point of it -- and because 'reported once per SITE' is a statement about the process, not about a caller. (2) g_b in editor/src/core/jce_editor_assert_bridge.cpp holds the one slot the handler records into plus its armed/pending flags, so a failure raised on any thread can be surfaced on the UI thread. IT LANDED AS TEN NAMES FIRST AND THIS DETECTOR CAUGHT IT: 857 -> 866. Folding each module into one struct gave 866 -> 859, which is exactly the lesson already recorded above for the 2026-09-08 text shape cache (six loose statics, 855->859 became 855->856) and the 2026-09-17 morph GPU module. IT ALSO APPEARED ONE COMMIT LATE, for the reason recorded above for g_cap in jce_scene_probe_capture.c: find_duplicate_symbols.py enumerates sources with 'git ls-files', so both new files were invisible to the detector while untracked and the audit that ran beside them was green on a tree that already contained them.  ||  2026-09-20 editor Automation door: ONE file-static, s_call in editor/src/core/jce_editor_automation.cpp, and it is already the folded form this detector asks for -- one struct holding the whole module (the JceProcess handle, the tool name, the envelope buffer, its length, and the truncation flag) rather than five loose names. It is the same shape as g_run in jce_run_manager.cpp, already inside the 859: a module that owns at most one child process at a time keeps that child in one place. ONE CALL IN FLIGHT IS NOT A SIMPLIFICATION -- the Automation layer takes a single-instance lock for anything that reaches the engine, and two concurrent calls through it exit without writing a result, which both call sites translate into INVALID_ARGS about arguments that were never wrong. Threading a handle through instead would mean a parameter on jce_editor_automation_call, on the per-frame poll the main loop makes, and on every future menu item -- to relocate one static out of a module whose whole job is to own one subprocess. IT APPEARED ONE COMMIT LATE, for the reason already recorded above for g_cap and for the assertion facility: find_duplicate_symbols.py enumerates sources with 'git ls-files', so the file was invisible while untracked and the audit that ran beside it was green on a tree that already contained it.  ||  2026-09-21 global-state 854 -> 855: s_matrix2d[32] in jce_physics_layers.c, the 2D collision matrix beside the 3D one. DECLARED BEFORE THE GATE FOUND IT, because the jce_scene_probe_capture.c shape is that a single-slot static goes green pre-commit and reddens the NEXT commit, charged to a change that does not own it. It is a fourth file-scope static in a module that already holds three (s_names, s_matrix, s_inited) and it is the same KIND as s_matrix: a process-wide cache of authored project settings, pushed in by jce_project_settings_push_physics_layers before any body spawns, never written by gameplay. Not merged into s_matrix because JceProjectSettings authors BOTH grids and the physics debugger draws both -- one shared matrix would delete a distinction the authoring surface already exposes, and Unity splits Physics from Physics2D the same way. Not made per-world because the 3D sibling is process-wide and the JSON bridge that carries it from cook to shipped runtime loads once in app_init; a per-world copy would need a second push path and two sources of truth for one authored fact.  ||  2026-09-22 global-state 855 -> 856: the insert-effect PLUGIN REGISTRY (jce_audio_dsp.c s_custom_registry). audio.dsp.insert-effect-chain is behind partly because 'Unity's is a plugin surface; this is a closed set', and a registry a project registers into at startup is process-global by nature -- per-chain registration would make every chain re-register the same effect, and a registry passed as a parameter would have to thread through jce_audio_dsp_chain_add, the mixer config parser and every caller of both. It is ONE object rather than the array-plus-counter it started as, so two globals cannot disagree and this costs one entry instead of two. Append-only and written only at startup before any audio thread reads it, which is what lets the audio-thread lookup take no lock.
_reasons.similar-code: 2026-09-21 similar-code 66 -> 67: jce_curve_channel_index() is token-identical to jce_anim_sm_param_find() -- "linear scan an array of named entries, return the index or -1", 53 tokens, five lines. They share a SHAPE and no state, no invariant and no layer: one is in middleware/animation over JceAnimSmParam, the other in resource over the curve's Channel, and the two element types have nothing in common but a char name[]. Unifying them means a void*+stride+offsetof helper in jce_core (jce_name_index(base, stride, name_off, count, name)), which trades five obviously-correct lines for a call the compiler cannot type-check and whose failure mode -- a wrong member offset -- reads the wrong bytes silently. That is a worse artefact, and creating a core dependency for two call sites in two layers to host it is worse again. Recorded rather than dissolved, and recorded rather than reshaped: rewriting the loop through jce_curve_channel_name() would drop the count by changing the token sequence while leaving exactly the same code, which is gaming the detector instead of answering it.
